subject: armadillo
pitch: A nine-banded armadillo trotting along. A shell of overlapping banded plates in dusty pinkish-tan, a pointy snout, tall leathery ears, small beady eyes, sturdy clawed feet and a long armoured tail tapering to a point. A sprinkle of coarse pale hairs pokes out between the bands.
reasoning:
I'm planning out the armadillo's skeleton structure, sketching joint positions for the pelvis, spine chain, neck, head, tail, and the four legs facing +Z with left as +X.

For the shell, I'm figuring out how to build banded plates by sweeping short overlapping tube sections along the spine with a radius function that flares slightly toward the rear of each band, creating a shingled armor look.

Now I'm mapping the spine path itself — a curved line from shoulders to hips through four points, with a root joint near the pelvis, and I need to decide whether to use a polyline or catmull-rom curve for smoothness through those joints.

For body thickness, I'm defining a radius profile along that spine using a sine-based taper so the shell bulges widest around the middle and narrows toward both the front (shoulder shield) and rear (pelvic shield), with separate x/y scaling for an elliptical cross-section.

For coloring, I'm planning a countershading approach: tan/darker bands painted on top for the shell, pale underside for the belly, plus some mottling, using sweep gradients to apply the color transitions along the body.

Working out band paint colors with mottled tan texture and belly shading, plus a radius function to taper each of the nine shell bands with slight overlap for flare. Thinking through cap geometry so the band tube ends don't show an unwanted flat disk at the rear.

Planning the sweep settings next: ten sides per ring to keep the mesh low-poly, then starting to lay out the neck chain joints from spine to snout tip for the head shape.

Still shaping the head geometry...

Shaping the ear outline as a tall rounded silhouette, thin in depth, tilted slightly outward and back from the head.

Setting ear x-offset to ±0.032. For legs, I'm planning a simple 3-joint chain per leg (shoulder, elbow, wrist tip) with approximate hip/foot positions for a neutral standing pose, defining the polyline paths for each limb.

Now I'm sweeping the leg chain with a tapered radius for a sturdy tapered look, then adding paw geometry as a flat box foot with three forward-facing claw spikes positioned so their tips touch the floor.

I'm switching the foot shape to a scaled sphere so it sits flush with the ground, then laying out the hind leg joints—hip, knee, ankle—on each side to mirror the front leg structure.

Now I'm checking that leg attachment points sit properly inside the body's curved silhouette, adjusting hip and shoulder positions so the limbs visually connect rather than floating outside the torso.

For the tail, I'm plotting a tapering sequence of points running from the body's rear down to a thin tip, dividing it into three named segments and anchoring the chain to the nearest spine joint.

Adding slight overlap between tail bands to avoid visible gaps, then thinking about scattering hair-tuft texture cards across the body surface for added fur detail.

Blank texture should fall back fine with alphaTest, and I'll add some belly hair too, skipping sparse leg hair since it's not worth the complexity. For performance, triangle counts across all the bands stay low enough that scatter attempts remain cheap, and I'm now setting up the underlying body skin sweep along the spine chain with a dark pink base color and rounded caps.

For the shields, I'm working out cap types so the front shield gets a round start/flat end to form a visible plate near the head without exposing an awkward opening, while the rear shield uses a hidden flat start (tucked behind the previous flared band) and a round end.

Now I'm defining the texture and coloring for the shields and bands, using scale-tile patterns with tan tones and countershading toward the belly color to give them depth.

For the legs, I'm setting up a mottled skin tone with small size variation, and considering adding a few small flattened scutes near the front of the legs for extra texture detail.

Pose stays neutral rather than trotting. Now I'm working out the eyes, nostrils as tiny dark spheres, and the jaw joint placement so the mouth sweep runs properly from the head toward the snout.

Checking the head-to-shield overlap, I realize the head's base radius is wider than the dome opening, so the head emerges oddly from the shield -- I need to pull the spine start back to around z=0.12 so the dome edge clears the head properly.

Still positioning facial geometry...

Setting up the joint hierarchy now: jaw joint near the head, neck joint at the spine base aiming toward the head with spine1 as its parent, and a root joint anchoring the chain. I'm laying out the spine points across three segments from the base up to the neck.

Now I'm working through the body's radius profile along the spine, placing bands and the hind leg at the correct z positions, then checking that the tail emerges correctly from inside the rear dome where the body tapers off, defining the tail's path points as it extends backward and downward.

Writing tapered band helper...

Still writing hair strand paths...

I'm checking color saturation thresholds to classify the hair tone as coloured rather than tinted, then setting up scatter logic to distribute hair strands across the upper surface with minimum spacing, plus confirming cards stay within the mesh part limit before moving to claws.

Now I'm defining each foot's three claws as spike shapes with offset bases, direction vectors, and bone attachments tied to wrist/ankle joint names for front and hind legs, then starting the leg-building function with its parameters.

Still writing leg function...

Mirroring foot and bone positions with x-flip for symmetry, keeping colors consistent, and noting the 64-color flat palette limit is fine for mottled leg skin. I'm typing the radius function to return a tuple and finishing up with the ear extrusion parameters—position, axes, thickness, bevel, and bone attachment to the head.

Now I'm shaping the ear outline points and tuning smoothing for rounded edges, adjusting the flare direction so the tilt works correctly after projecting onto the x-axis, and then building the inner ear by scaling and offsetting the outline with its own thickness and color.
